subject: Escalation: Private customer missing RBAC audit events (SUP-18421) — patch plan + timeline
body:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Escalation: Private customer missing RBAC audit events (SUP-18421) — patch plan + timeline

Looping in Product/Platform/GRC per escalation SOP.

We have an enterprise Private customer (Helio Bank) reporting missing audit log events for RBAC changes in their Private deployment. Support ticket: SUP-18421.

Symptoms (per Support + customer samples):
- They see auth/login and some config events, but *no RBAC change events* when creating/editing roles and when adding users to groups.
- They expect event_type(s) like rbac.role.created / rbac.role.updated / rbac.assignment.updated (names vary in their notes), but the stream is quiet.
- They are exporting to Splunk and trying to meet internal audit requirements for admin activity.

Impact:
- Blocks security review sign-off. They’re asking for written confirmation + patch ETA.

Asks:
1) Platform: confirm whether this is a control-plane emitter gap vs. audit pipeline/exporter issue in Private.
2) SRE: confirm if any ingestion/backlog/drop behavior could explain selective missing types.
3) Product (Private): confirm acceptable customer messaging + mitigation (workaround) until patch.

Customer-provided artifacts (redacted):
- Attached: heliobank-private-audit-samples-20260121.txt
- Attached: redwood-private-values-redacted.yaml (their exporter config snippet)

Proposed plan (draft):
- Triage today, confirm root cause, and ship a Private hotfix within 7–10 days.
- If this is “missing instrumentation” in the Private installer/control plane, prioritize backport.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering (Exec Owner)
Redwood Inference


---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 9:38 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Private customer missing RBAC audit events (SUP-18421) — patch plan + timeline

Thanks Marcus.

From Private POV: we can’t leave “RBAC changes not audited” unresolved. If it’s a known gap, we need an explicit remediation timeline and a temporary risk acceptance (time-bounded) documented.

Two questions:
- What Private version are they on (app + installer)?
- Are they using the embedded exporter or external sidecar?

If we can get an ETA by EOD tomorrow, I’ll coordinate customer comms with Support/Solutions.

Vivek
Product — Private Deployments


---

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 10:11 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Private customer missing RBAC audit events (SUP-18421) — patch plan + timeline

I skimmed the samples.

They’re receiving events with schema_version missing/blank and some legacy fields. That suggests the exporter is passing through mixed producers and not normalizing (or normalization is disabled).

Two quick notes:
- In the samples, event_source looks like "console" and "gateway", but I do not see any "control-plane" producer identifier.
- Their config shows exporter enabled, but the control-plane audit sink may not be wired (depends on values in private chart).

I can help correlate against the coverage dashboard patterns we’ve seen: when control-plane audit sink is misconfigured, you’ll see exactly what they see (UI activity without RBAC change events).

Can someone confirm their private values block for audit sink wiring? (Looks like it’s partially redacted.)

Aisha
Platform Observability


---

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Private customer missing RBAC audit events (SUP-18421) — patch plan + timeline

I asked the Platform on-call to take a first pass (can’t join the thread directly).

Hypothesis from a similar internal repro last week:
- In Private v1.14.0, RBAC endpoints *do* emit audit events, but only if the control-plane audit sink env vars are set (AUDIT_SINK_URL / AUDIT_TOPIC / etc.)
- Installer chart defaults were updated and we may have a missing value mapping in some upgrade paths (existing installs don’t get the new sink settings).

If that holds, the fix is either:
1) Doc/workaround: customer sets the sink values manually in their Helm values + restart control-plane.
2) Patch: private-installer backport to ensure sink wiring is applied on upgrade and validated.

Marcus: can you ask Support for their exact versions + whether this started after upgrade?

Priya
Platform Engineering (Sponsor)


---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 11:26 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Private customer missing RBAC audit events (SUP-18421) — patch plan + timeline

Got it.

Support update (from SUP-18421 notes):
- Private app: 1.14.0
- Installer: 0.18.2
- Issue noticed immediately after upgrading from 1.13.x → 1.14.0 (they were doing validation for Splunk export)

They’re using embedded audit-log-exporter and shipping to Splunk HEC.

If the workaround is “set sink values manually + restart control-plane,” we need:
- exact keys/paths in values.yaml
- confirmation this doesn’t break their supportability posture
- language we can share (and whether we need to treat this as a security incident vs. product bug)

Naomi/Olga: from control standpoint, is “temporary gap + mitigation + hotfix ETA” acceptable for SOC2 conversations?

Marcus

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 12:04 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Private customer missing RBAC audit events (SUP-18421) — patch plan + timeline

For SOC 2 / ISO-aligned discussions: yes, “temporary gap + documented workaround + committed remediation date” can be acceptable, but we must be precise.

Minimum requirements for external wording:
- Acknowledge that specific admin actions (RBAC changes) were not being exported due to configuration/upgrade wiring.
- Provide an immediate mitigation (customer action) and a near-term patch to prevent recurrence.
- Avoid implying “guaranteed delivery” if we’re still operating at best-effort semantics in Private.
- Capture this as an exception/waiver with an expiry if we can’t patch quickly.

If we provide a workaround, please ensure it is reviewed for risk (no new secrets logged; does not require disabling auth).

Olga
GRC

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 12:33 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Private customer missing RBAC audit events (SUP-18421) — patch plan + timeline

Agree with Olga.

From Product/Security posture:
- Treat as a Sev-2 customer-blocking defect (not a security incident) unless we see evidence of tampering/unauthorized access.
- We should not frame it as “audit logs are complete” for Private until patch is deployed; instead: “audit events for RBAC changes were not being emitted/exported under a specific Private upgrade configuration; we have a mitigation and a patch scheduled.”

Marcus: once we have root cause, I’ll draft customer-facing language for Support to reuse across security review questions.

Naomi
Product — Security & Compliance

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 23, 2026 at 9:17 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Private customer missing RBAC audit events (SUP-18421) — patch plan + timeline

Update after engineering review (summarizing the internal triage):

Root cause (confirmed):
- Control-plane RBAC endpoints are emitting v1 audit events in 1.14.0.
- In Private, the control-plane audit sink wiring was not applied on upgrade for certain Helm value shapes (legacy installs). Result: control-plane events never reached the exporter.
- Exporter continued to export gateway/console events, so the stream looked “healthy,” but RBAC changes were missing.

Mitigation (customer can do today):
- Add the control-plane audit sink configuration to their values.yaml (we’ll provide exact stanza) and restart control-plane pods.
- After restart, they should see RBAC events within minutes.

Patch plan:
- Backport a fix to private-installer to validate sink wiring during upgrade and fail with a clear preflight error if audit sink is not configured (instead of silently dropping).
- Target hotfix: Private installer 0.18.3 + app patch 1.14.1 (if needed; may be installer-only).

Timeline (tentative):
- PR ready for review: Mon 1/26
- Build + QA: Tue–Wed 1/27–1/28
- Customer delivery: Thu 1/29 (subject to validation)

Marcus: OK to communicate mitigation immediately via Support; patch ETA can be shared as “week of Jan 26.”

Priya


---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Jan 24, 2026 at 4:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Private customer missing RBAC audit events (SUP-18421) — patch plan + timeline

Thanks all. Next steps I’m taking (for visibility):

1) Support response (SUP-18421)
- Sending the mitigation stanza + restart instructions with a note that this is a known upgrade wiring issue.
- Asking them to confirm once RBAC events appear in Splunk (include a sample event_id/time for verification).

2) Engineering tracking
- Linking this escalation to the Private instrumentation/parity work (ENG-4826) and exporter normalization (ENG-4827) so we don’t regress.
- Requesting we add an automated preflight check in the installer so this can’t silently happen again.

3) Customer-facing language
- Naomi: I’ll sync with you on wording to ensure we don’t over-claim delivery semantics, and to document this as a time-bounded exception if needed.

4) Evidence/controls
- Olga: once mitigation is confirmed, we can capture a before/after sample set for audit readiness (RBAC role update event + export proof).

If anything slips on the Jan 29 target, flag me immediately; Helio is gating their sign-off on this.

Marcus

(Attachment referenced for Support: redwood-private-values-redacted.yaml)
